stem: Which three steps are repeated on every pass of a game loop?

options.content: Read the input, update the state, show the output
options.rationale: Each pass handles one step of the game.

options.content: Save the file, close the file, delete the file
options.rationale: Those are file operations.

options.content: Compile, link, run
options.rationale: Those steps build a program.

options.content: Define, declare, return
options.rationale: Those are programming terms, not game-loop steps.

explanation: A game loop repeats input, update and output.

stem: Which of these is part of the game state?

options.content: The player's score
options.rationale: The score describes the game at that moment.

options.content: The programming language used
options.rationale: That is a decision made before the game is run.

options.content: The colour of the programmer's screen
options.rationale: It is not part of the game.

options.content: The name of the file the game is saved in
options.rationale: That is not part of the game's situation.

explanation: State = positions, score, lives and stage.

stem: What is the purpose of collision detection in a game?

options.content: To make the game run on more than one phone
options.rationale: That is portability.

options.content: To store the score in a file
options.rationale: That is file handling.

options.content: To stop the player from quitting the game
options.rationale: That is not collision detection.

options.content: To find when two objects are in the same place
options.rationale: For example collecting an item or losing a life.

stem: A weather app asks for permission to use the phone's location. What is the best reason for this?

options.content: To send the user's contacts to the developer
options.rationale: Contacts are not needed for a forecast.

options.content: To show the forecast for the place where the user is
options.rationale: The permission is needed for a feature of the app.

options.content: To make the screen brighter
options.rationale: Location does not control brightness.

options.content: To save battery
options.rationale: Using location uses more battery.

stem: Why is it useful for a school app to work offline?

options.content: Offline apps need no battery power at all to run
options.rationale: All apps use the battery.

options.content: It still works when the connection is poor
options.rationale: Data is stored on the phone and synchronised later.

options.content: Offline apps cannot be copied to another phone
options.rationale: That is not related to being offline.

options.content: Offline apps can use any amount of the phone memory
options.rationale: The memory of the phone is limited.

explanation: Offline use keeps the app working when there is no connection.

stem: Which design decision best reduces the data cost of a news app for users with small data bundles?

options.content: Play a video on the home screen as soon as it opens
options.rationale: Video uses a lot of data.

options.content: Download every article again each time the app opens
options.rationale: That uses data repeatedly.

options.content: Show text first and load images only on request
options.rationale: Text needs far less data than images.

options.content: Refresh the whole screen every second for new content
options.rationale: Constant refreshing uses data and battery.

explanation: Low-data design uses text first, compression and caching.
hints: Which content uses the least data?

stem: Which feature is characteristic of a mobile app rather than a desktop program?

options.content: Input only by a keyboard and mouse
options.rationale: That describes a desktop.

options.content: A very large screen
options.rationale: Phones have small screens.

options.content: No use of sensors
options.rationale: Phones have sensors such as GPS.

options.content: Input by touch on a small screen
options.rationale: Taps and swipes replace the mouse.

explanation: Mobile apps are designed for touch and small screens.

stem: A game loop must contain a condition that can end it, such as the number of lives reaching zero.
explanation: True. Without an end condition the loop would repeat for ever.

stem: An app should ask for every permission that the phone offers, in case it needs them later.
explanation: False. An app should ask only for the permissions needed for its features.

stem:
A game checks three pairs of rectangles, each described by (x, y, width, height), for collisions. Rectangles that only touch along an edge do not collide.

| Pair | Rectangle A | Rectangle B |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| 1 | (0, 0, 4, 4) | (3, 3, 4, 4) |
| 2 | (0, 0, 4, 4) | (4, 0, 4, 4) |
| 3 | (2, 2, 2, 2) | (0, 0, 8, 8) |
How many of the pairs collide?
explanation: Pairs 1 and 3 collide; pair 2 only touches.
workedSolution: Pair 1: A covers x 0 to 4 and y 0 to 4, B covers x 3 to 7 and y 3 to 7, so they overlap. Pair 2: A ends at x = 4 where B starts, so they only touch. Pair 3: A is inside B, so they overlap. Two pairs collide.
hints: Two rectangles collide when they overlap in both directions; touching edges do not count.

stem: Explain what happens in the game loop of a simple game. [3]

points.description: The loop repeats while the game is not over
On each pass the program reads the player's input and updates the game state (movement, collisions, score)
It then shows the new state to the player

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The loop repeats until the game is over. On each pass it reads the input, updates the state (movement, collisions, score) and shows the new state to the player.

stem: Design a mobile app that shows the daily market prices of vegetables to farmers who have small data bundles and unreliable connections. Describe four features of the design. [4]

points.description: Screens: a home screen with a list of vegetables and a price screen for each, with simple navigation
Large buttons and clear text for touch input on small screens
Prices are stored on the phone and updated when a connection is available, so the app works offline
Low-data design: text only, compressed data and no large images or video

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A home screen lists the vegetables and a price screen shows each one. Buttons and text are large for touch input. The latest prices are stored on the phone and updated when a connection is available, so the app works offline. Only text is downloaded, to keep data use low.

explanation: Link the features to the users and conditions.
hints: Screens, input, stored data and low-data design.

stem: Explain why an app should request only the permissions it needs. [2]

points.description: Each permission gives the app access to personal data or hardware (such as location or contacts), which is a risk to the user's privacy
Users trust the app less, and may refuse to install it, if it asks for permissions that its features do not need

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Permissions give access to personal data or hardware, which risks the user's privacy, and users trust an app less if it asks for more than its features need.

hints: Think about the user's privacy and trust.

stem: In a game the variable `Lives` starts at 3 and the variable `Position` is the player's cell. Write pseudocode for the part of the game loop that reduces the lives by 1 and outputs a message if the player's cell is 4, and ends the loop when the lives reach 0. [3]

points.description: A selection testing Position = 4
Lives ← Lives - 1 and an output message inside the selection
A loop condition (WHILE Lives > 0, or an equivalent test) that ends the loop when the lives reach 0

answerSpec.markingNotes:
Example answer: ```
WHILE Lives > 0 DO
    // read the input and move the player here
    IF Position = 4 THEN
        Lives ← Lives - 1
        OUTPUT "You hit a hazard"
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE
```

explanation: A collision test and the end condition.
hints: Use an IF inside the loop.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State the first line of output.
parts.explanation: The third R moves the player to cell 3, which has a thorn bush.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State the second line of output.
parts.explanation: The fourth R moves the player to cell 4, which has a prize.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: State the values in the last line of output.
parts.explanation: One thorn bush costs a life (2 - 1 = 1), the prize gives 5, and there were 5 turns, the last ending the game at cell 5.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain why the loop condition includes `position < 5`.

points.description: Cell 5 is the end of the path, so reaching it finishes the game
Without this condition the loop would carry on asking for moves after the end of the path

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Cell 5 is the end of the path, so the game finishes when the player reaches it. Without the condition the loop would keep asking for moves.

parts.explanation: The loop needs an end condition for winning as well as losing.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Identify the lines that carry out the collision detection in the program.

points.description: The two if statements that test whether position is in hazards and whether it is in prizes

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The statements `if position in hazards` and `if position in prizes`.

parts.explanation: They test whether the player is in the same cell as an object.

explanation: Tracing a game loop with lives, hazards and prizes.
hints: Follow the position after each move.
The loop stops when lives are 0 or the position reaches 5.

stem: A clinic in Mutare wants a mobile app that reminds mothers of the dates of their children's vaccinations. Many mothers have basic smartphones, small data bundles and a poor signal.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Describe two screens of the app and what each one shows.

points.description: A home screen listing the children with the date of the next vaccination for each
A detail screen for one child with the vaccinations already given and those still due

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A home screen lists each child with the next vaccination date. A detail screen for one child shows the vaccinations given and those still due.

parts.explanation: Each screen has one clear job.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain how the app can work when there is no signal.

points.description: The children's records and dates are stored on the phone
Reminders are shown by the phone at the stored dates, and changes are synchronised when a connection becomes available

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The records and dates are stored on the phone, so the reminders can be shown without a signal, and any changes are synchronised when a connection is available.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: State one permission the app may need and the reason.

points.description: Notifications, so that it can remind the mother on the day (or storage, to keep the records on the phone)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Notifications, so that it can remind the mother on the right day.

parts.explanation: Name the permission and the reason.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Give one way the design keeps the cost of data low.

points.description: The app downloads only small text updates and no images or video

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It downloads only small text updates, not images or video.

explanation: Designing a mobile app for a described group of users.
hints: Use headings for the screens, inputs, data and permissions.
